worked_example_policy.include: Concrete numerical instances with a worked numerical answer, computed solution plot or substantive numerical experiment in the main text. Include tiny explicit numerical answers even when obtained analytically. Include reported studies whose original data are missing, with that limitation recorded.
worked_example_policy.exclude: End-of-chapter exercises; arbitrary-data symbolic derivations; generic modeling examples without a numerical result; pure definitions/function plots and conceptual diagrams. Numerical companion instantiations alone do not turn symbolic textbook examples into numerical worked examples.
worked_example_policy.grouping: A numbered Example is one entry; related figures for the same numerical study are grouped. Different algorithms on a reused instance may have separate entries when presented as separate studies. Entry count is a study count, not a figure count.
worked_example_policy.status: Every entry starts pending. Data/code availability and catalog completion are not reproduction completion. Verified implementations are tracked separately.
worked_example_policy.exactness: Exact_data_available concerns published instance inputs, not numerical verification or pixel identity. Official_seeded_generator requires legacy MATLAB RNG semantics; the same NumPy integer seed is insufficient. A method-only reproduction must disclose substituted data.

entries.title: Scalar optimal values, attainment, and unboundedness
expected_outputs: For f(x)=1/x on x>0: infimum 0, not attained.
For f(x)=-log(x) on x>0: objective unbounded below, infimum -infinity.
For f(x)=x log(x) on x>0: unique minimizer x*=1/e approximately 0.3678794412; optimal value -1/e approximately -0.3678794412.
entries.data_availability: All three scalar objective functions and their common domain x>0 are explicitly supplied.
entries.verification_requirement: Run an independent implementation, save input provenance and outputs, check feasibility/optimality or stated analytic benchmark, and disclose all data substitutions/source discrepancies before marking verified.
entries.reproduction_basis: For x>0, compare 1/x, -log(x), and x log(x). The first tends to zero as x tends to infinity and remains positive, so the infimum is not attained. The second decreases without bound. The last has derivative 1+log(x) and positive second derivative 1/x, so its unique minimum is x=1/e, with value -1/e. A bounded scalar optimizer independently checks this last value.
